When this had been said, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha: "O Son of the Conqueror, oh, this assembly is utterly pure; these are Bodhisattvas who have perfectly purified their superior intention, perfectly purified their conceptual thinking, perfectly practiced what is to be practiced, made offerings to many billions of Buddhas, perfectly accumulated the collections, are endowed with immeasurable qualities, are free from hesitation and doubt, are without afflictions, are well-established in superior intention and conviction, and are a gathering consisting entirely of those who are not dependent on others regarding these Buddha-dharma." Therefore, regarding the statement: "O Son of the Conqueror, since these Bodhisattvas are entirely those who abide in this state through direct perception, please explain it well," why did the noble Vimukticandra praise that assembly? It was to show that "even if such individuals are rare in the world, they are present in this assembly." In that regard, "perfectly purified superior intention" is a branch. That perfectly purified superior intention should be understood as twofold: purity of transmission and purity of realization. Purity of retention by holding many undistorted teachings for a long time is what is meant by "made offerings to many billions of Buddhas." **Fascicle Two.**

When he had spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said this to the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha: 

"O Son of the Conqueror! Alas! This assembly is perfectly pure. These Bodhisattvas have perfectly purified their high resolve, perfectly purified their conceptions, and perfectly practiced what is to be practiced. They have made offerings to many billions of Buddhas. They have perfectly gathered the accumulations and possess immeasurable virtues. They are free from doubt and hesitation. They are without afflictions. They abide firmly in high resolve and devotion. They are a gathering solely of those who do not depend on others regarding these Buddha-dharmas. Therefore, O Son of the Conqueror, since these Bodhisattvas are solely those who abide in the direct perception of this state, please explain it well!"

If one asks: why does the noble Vimukticandra praise that assembly? It is to show that although such individuals are rare in the world, they are indeed present in this assembly. Regarding that, "perfectly purified high resolve" is the primary limb. This perfectly purified high resolve should be known in two ways: purity of scripture and purity of realization. 

Purity of scripture is of five types. First, the purity of interest for the sake of conceiving the means to obtain the desired scripture is said: "because their conceptions are perfectly purified." 

Second, the purity of seeking by practicing the conduct of body and speech consistent with obtaining that is said: "because they have perfectly practiced what is to be practiced." 

Third, the purity of retention by holding many non-erroneous teachings for a long time is said: "because they have made offerings to many billions of Buddhas." 

Fourth, obtaining the distinction of mindfulness in successive lifetimes through the distinction of aspiration; thus, purity of what is obtained by birth...
